bio.en: Ethan Smith is the CEO of Graphite, a leading SEO and answer-engine-optimization (AEO) agency, and one of the most sought-after experts on how to get products to show up as answers inside LLMs like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. With 18 years of SEO experience dating back to 2007, he advises many top B2B SaaS and e-commerce companies on capturing the fast-growing answer-engine channel.
bio.zh: Ethan Smith 是 Graphite 的 CEO，一家领先的 SEO 与答案引擎优化（AEO）机构，也是关于"如何让产品作为答案出现在 ChatGPT、Gemini、Perplexity 这类 LLM 里"最抢手的专家之一。他拥有自 2007 年起 18 年的 SEO 经验，为许多顶级 B2B SaaS 和电商公司提供顾问，帮它们抓住这个快速增长中的答案引擎渠道。

summary.en: AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) is about getting your product cited as an answer inside LLMs; it's closely related to SEO, but the "head" (you must be mentioned as many times as possible across the summarized answer, not just rank #1) and the far larger, longer "tail" of follow-up questions work differently. Most levers overlap with traditional SEO—landing pages, YouTube videos, Reddit, affiliates, and help-center optimization—but you also need offsite citation optimization and must answer every follow-up question on your own pages; unlike Google, early-stage companies can win quickly because a citation can make them show up immediately. Track "share of voice" with an answer tracker across the few high-traffic LLM surfaces, run controlled experiments (test vs. control groups) since most published best practices are unproven, and treat Reddit by being a genuine, helpful user rather than spamming. He also warns that 100% AI-generated content does not work—it drives model collapse and gets filtered—while AI-assisted, human-edited content is the future, and that the core technology is similar enough to SEO that the "everything has changed" hype is mostly misinformation.

So same thing with ChatGPT, anything can be optimized, but if you're spamming it, they'll see that. (00:09:43): And they'll have a whole team looking at that and then they'll change your algorithm to prevent you from doing that.
turns.zh: 对。我既同意也不同意，但我思考的方式是：任何东西都可以被优化。你只需要理解底层的系统和游戏规则，如果你做到了，你就能优化任何东西。你能优化算法、能优化人，任何东西都能被优化。我觉得他大概的意思是两件事。一是："求你别往我产品里塞垃圾。"二是："如果你塞了，我会看到、而且我会阻止你那么做。"所以制造垃圾不是个长期、稳健的策略，就像在 Google 上制造垃圾也不是长期、稳健的策略一样。最终，Google 会说："那些巨大的购物比价网站在做一亿个自动生成的搜索页面，我不喜欢，我要把整个品类干掉。"ChatGPT 也是一样，任何东西都能被优化，但如果你在塞垃圾，他们会看到的。而且他们会有一整个团队盯着这个，然后他们会改算法来阻止你那么做。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What kind of impact have you seen? You've done work with a lot of companies, we'll talk through a few examples. (00:09:53): Maybe share one to give us context just like how much can you impact this sort of thing where you show up in, say, ChatGPT more often?
turns.zh: 你见过什么样的影响？你跟很多公司做过合作，我们待会儿会聊几个例子。也许先分享一个，给我们点背景——就这种"让你更频繁地出现在，比如 ChatGPT 里"的事，你到底能产生多大的影响？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: You can affect it a lot. So a specific example with Webflow is we are working with Webflow on their SEO. We're working on their content, and we're seeing a lot of wins on the Answer Engine Optimization side. (00:10:16): So the specific things that we've done there, one is just traditional SEO. So make landing pages for high-search volume keywords, like best no-code website designer. (00:10:28): And then for free, you'll get Answer Engine Optimization impact from that. So that's just traditional SEO, which works very well for AEO.
turns.zh: 你能影响很多。拿 Webflow 的具体例子来说，我们在帮 Webflow 做 SEO。我们在做他们的内容，而且在答案引擎优化那一侧看到很多成效。我们在那儿做的具体事情，一是就是传统的 SEO。就是为高搜索量的关键词做落地页，比如"最好的无代码网站设计工具"。然后免费地，你就能从中获得答案引擎优化的效果。所以那就是传统 SEO，而它对 AEO 非常管用。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I was just going to say, that sounds exactly the same as regular SEO.
turns.zh: 我正想说，这听起来跟普通 SEO 一模一样啊。

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Yeah. So I would say everything that works in SEO works in AEO, but there are additional things beyond SEO that also work in AEO. So second thing, and the way that I think about AEO versus SEO is that the head and the tail are different. So the head is different in that in order to win something like what's the best website builder? (00:10:59): Even if Webflow's URL shows up number one on the citations, they're not going to win the answer because their URL showed up number one, but at Google they would win. If their blue link showed up first they would win, but that's not the case in the LLM. Because the LLM is summarizing many citations and so you need to get mentioned as many times as possible. (00:11:18): So usually when you ask something like, "What's the best tool for X?" The first answer will be mentioned the most in the citations, because that's very different from Google. And so for Webflow, we work with them on YouTube videos, Vimeo videos, getting mentioned in Reddit, getting mentioned in other blogs, affiliates, stuff like that. (00:11:39): So tried a bunch of stuff. Stuff that worked especially well was just straight SEO, number one. Number two is YouTube videos, and then the third is Reddit optimization.
turns.zh: 对。所以我会说，SEO 里管用的东西在 AEO 里都管用，但还有超出 SEO 之外的东西在 AEO 里也管用。第二件事——我是这么区分 AEO 和 SEO 的：头部（head）和尾部（tail）是不一样的。头部不一样的地方在于，要赢下"最好的建站工具是哪个"这种问题。哪怕 Webflow 的 URL 在引用来源里排第一，他们也不一定能赢下那个答案——因为是他们 URL 排第一，但在 Google 上他们就赢了。如果他们的蓝链排第一他们就赢了，但在 LLM 里不是这样。因为 LLM 是在总结很多引用来源，所以你得被提到的次数尽可能多。通常当你问"X 最好的工具是哪个"这种问题时，排第一的那个答案会在引用里被提到最多，因为那跟 Google 非常不一样。所以对 Webflow，我们跟他们在 YouTube 视频、Vimeo 视频、在 Reddit 被提到、在其他博客被提到、affiliates 等等上合作。所以试了一堆东西。特别管用的，第一就是纯 SEO。第二是 YouTube 视频，第三是 Reddit 优化。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay, wow. So you're saying if you can get to number one, when you ask ChatGPT, "What's the best website builder?" (00:11:54): And Webflow's at the top, that doesn't actually drive them as much traffic as simply being mentioned most often across the summary?
turns.zh: 好，哇。所以你的意思是，如果你问 ChatGPT"最好的建站工具是哪个"、能让 Webflow 排到第一，那其实带来的流量，还不如它只是在整个摘要里被提到次数最多？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Yes. And part of why that's interesting is because when startups come to me and ask me for SEO help, my first response is, "Don't do it at all. Spend your time on something else because you're not going to be able to grow SEO early on in search." Because you don't have enough domain authority and it takes a while to get domain authority, and only once you have domain authority can you rank. (00:12:23): And so for Google, it's usually something that you do Series A, Series B or later. You don't do it as soon as you start because can't win early on. That's not the case for Answer Engine Optimization, because you can get mentioned by a citation tomorrow and start showing up immediately. You can have a Reddit thread, you can have a YouTube video. (00:12:42): You can be mentioned on a blog, like a brand-new YC company launches, everyone's talking about them. They could show up in an answer tomorrow as a result of that. So early-stage companies can win, they can win quickly. And they can win quickly and anyone can win quickly, by getting mentioned as many times as possible by the citations. So that's what's different about the head. (00:13:04): What's different about the tail is that the tail is larger in chat than in search. So the average number of words, I think, Perplexity said this to somebody else, said that it was around 25 words, where versus Google words it's around six words. So the tail is just much, much larger. People are asking lots of follow-up questions.
turns.zh: 对。而这之所以有意思，部分原因是：当初创来找我要 SEO 帮助时，我的第一反应是"别做。把时间花在别的事上，因为你在搜索里早期根本做不起来 SEO。"因为你没有足够的域名权重（domain authority），而积累域名权重要时间，只有有了域名权重你才能排上名。所以对 Google 来说，这通常是从 A 轮、B 轮或更晚才开始做的事。你不会一启动就做，因为早期赢不了。但在答案引擎优化里不是这样，因为你明天就可能被一个引用来源提到、然后马上开始出现。你可以是一条 Reddit 帖子、可以是一个 YouTube 视频。你可以在一篇博客里被提到，比如一家全新的 YC 公司发布，大家都在聊他们。结果他们明天就可能出现在某个答案里。所以早期公司能赢，而且能赢得很快。任何人都能赢得很快，只要通过被引用来源尽可能多地提到。所以这就是头部不一样的地方。尾部不一样的地方是：在对话里尾部比在搜索里大得多。平均词数，我觉得 Perplexity 跟别人说过，大概是 25 个词，而 Google 那边大概是 6 个词。所以尾部要大得多得多。人们在问大量的后续问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The tail, the prompt essentially, the question you're asking?
turns.zh: 尾部，本质上就是那个 prompt，就是你在问的问题？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Yes. Meaning that if you map out all of the questions that people ask, kind of like an SEO, long-tail keywords, if you do long-tail questions, the size of the tail is larger. Meaning the amount of questions that are very specific is larger, the share and the volume. (00:13:42): And there's probably questions that have never been asked before and questions that have never been searched before, because search can't support lots of really specific, super-specific stuff. Whereas chat is specifically made to ask a bunch of follow-up questions and have a conversation. (00:13:58): And so there's all these questions that have never been asked or searched for before that are now being asked, and then you can win that. And when I got started in SEO, it was long-tail SEO where you have a page for every single keyword, which doesn't work anymore, but now the long tail is back in chat. (00:14:13): And if you know all those really specific questions that people are asking, you can also win that, and you can probably also win that early. And I've seen examples of early-stage companies who just launched some really specific AI-enabled payment processing API thing, and they will show up. And they'll show up because they're answering questions that's never been answered before.
turns.zh: 对。意思是，如果你把人们问的所有问题画成一张图——有点像 SEO 里的长尾关键词——如果你做长尾问题，尾部的体量更大。也就是说，非常具体的问题的数量、占比和量都更大。而且可能有以前从没被问过、也从没被搜过的问题，因为搜索支撑不了那么多真的非常具体、超级具体的内容。而对话（chat）就是专门为了问一堆后续问题、进行对话而造的。所以有一大堆以前从没被问过或搜过的问题，现在正在被问，而你可以赢下那些。我刚开始做 SEO 时，是长尾 SEO——每个关键词一个页面，那现在已经不灵了，但现在长尾在对话里又回来了。如果你知道人们问的那些真的非常具体的问题，你也能赢下那些，而且很可能还能在早期就赢。我见过早期公司的例子：他们刚发布了一个非常具体的、带 AI 的支付处理 API 之类的东西，他们就会冒出来。他们会冒出来，是因为他们在回答那些从没被回答过的问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Are the leads that these answer engines are driving to companies actually valuable? Are these good-quality leads for B2B SaaS especially?
turns.zh: 这些答案引擎带给公司的线索，真的有价值吗？尤其是对 B2B SaaS 来说，这些是高质量的线索吗？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: They are significantly more valuable. So Webflow, we saw a 6X conversion rate difference between LLM traffic and Google Search traffic.
turns.zh: 有价值得多。所以 Webflow 这边，我们看到 LLM 流量和 Google 搜索流量之间的转化率差了 6 倍。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Six times?
turns.zh: 六倍？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Six times so significantly more qualified. I think that's probably for a couple of reasons. Probably it's because you're so primed because you're having a conversation with multiple follow-ups, and so there's so much intent that you've built. (00:15:08): And you've probably really narrowed in on what you want, so when you're going somewhere, it's probably highly qualified. And so we're seeing that it's just a much higher conversion rate.
turns.zh: 六倍，所以质量高得多。我觉得这大概有几个原因。大概是因为你被"预热"得很充分，因为你在进行一场有多轮后续的对话，所以你建立起了非常强的意图。而且你可能已经真的把想要的东西收窄了，所以当你去某个地方时，那大概就是高度合格的。所以我们看到的就是转化率高出很多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, this is so interesting, and it makes sense. People trust ChatGPT to tell them the answer, and if you are the answer, you have so much advantage. Like that is what people want to know, and then, "Okay. Cool, thank you. I'm going to go check this out." (00:15:35): This all just makes sense. Going back to the three levers you shared, essentially it's the things that you see work in driving you showing up more in these answer engines, landing pages, YouTube videos and Reddit. Is that right?
turns.zh: 哇，这太有意思了，而且说得通。人们信任 ChatGPT 告诉他们答案，而如果你是那个答案，你就有了巨大的优势。就像那是人们想知道的，然后"好，酷，谢谢。我去看看这个。"这一切都说得通。回到你分享的三个杠杆——本质上就是那些你看到能驱动你更频繁出现在这些答案引擎里的东西：落地页、YouTube 视频和 Reddit。对吧？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Those are some of them.
turns.zh: 那只是其中一些。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: The other things, so I would break it up into stuff on your site, onsite and offsite. So onsite would be traditional SEO. The difference would be this long tail. I would also say that the difference is lots of follow-up questions about does your product do this thing? What are the use cases, features, integrations, languages? (00:16:07): Tell me about your product and really specific details about that and that's on your site. And then the second group would be offsite, which is show up in all the citations. Citations are comprised of video, UGC like Reddit and Quora, affiliates. (00:16:23): Dotdash Meredith is showing up all over the place, Glamour, Good Housekeeping, it's like getting mentioned there, blogs, so it's those two groups.
turns.zh: 还有别的，所以我会把它拆成你网站上的东西——站内（onsite）和站外（offsite）。站内的就是传统 SEO。不一样的地方在于这个长尾。我还想说，不一样的是大量后续问题，比如"你的产品有没有这个功能？"用例是什么、功能是什么、集成是什么、支持什么语言？告诉我你的产品，以及关于它的真的非常具体的细节——这些是在你网站上的。然后第二组是站外，也就是在所有引用来源里出现。引用来源包括视频、UGC 比如 Reddit 和 Quora、affiliates。Dotdash Meredith 到处出现，Glamour、Good Housekeeping 那种，就是在那儿被提到，还有博客，所以就是这两组。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And that all sounds very similar to SEO showing up on other people's pages. Showing links from, say, Reddit is always great. (00:16:41): It's interesting that Reddit is such a big deal. What's going on there do you think?
turns.zh: 那听起来跟 SEO 出现在别人页面上非常像。比如来自 Reddit 的链接总是很好。有意思的是 Reddit 居然这么重要。你觉得那儿是怎么回事？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Okay, Reddit is one of the most interesting things. It's hugely cited in LLMs. And it's probably the number one thing people are asking, customers are asking me is, "How do we optimize for Reddit?" And this goes back to the head of ChatGPT's question about, "Please don't spam my product." (00:17:06): And so Reddit is a community where it's real opinions from people, authentic, and it's heavily managed by the community and the community is very good at managing it. And so the obvious strategy for a growth person is, "Let's make a bunch of automated spam and spam Reddit all over the place and get my product to show up everywhere." (00:17:27): That's the growth mindset, which makes sense, the hustle mindset. So what are people looking at? They're looking at creating hundreds of fake Reddit accounts pretending to be someone that you're not. I have a single person, I'm going to make 100 Reddit accounts. I'm going to autopost comments and then like my own comments. (00:17:46): And then build a trust score, and then shout, say everywhere that my product is the best product. Fortunately, that doesn't work very well, but that's the obvious strategy. And so we're seeing people trying to do that and then we're also seeing those accounts get banned, those comments get deleted. And so we're seeing people trying to spam and being unsuccessful, so that's one strategy. (00:18:05): The other strategy is the whole purpose of Reddit is to post useful, high-quality, authentic comments from real people. So at Webflow, we have a couple of people at Webflow going to comments and saying, "This is my name, this is where I work, and here's a useful piece of information." So the strategy is find a thread that is a part of a citation that you want to show up in. (00:18:30): Say who you are, say where you work, and then give a useful piece of information, and that works really well. And that sounds simple if you're not in the growth mindset of, "I need to scale this to hundreds of comments." But you don't actually need 10,000 comments, even five could be great and that scales perfectly well. (00:18:47): So the Reddit strategy is the obvious strategy, which is just to be an actual user of Reddit. Make an account, say who you are, say where you work, and give a useful answer.
turns.zh: 好，Reddit 是最有意思的东西之一。它在 LLM 里被大量引用。而且它大概是大家、客户问我最多的问题："我们怎么针对 Reddit 做优化？"这就回到了 ChatGPT 负责人那个"求你别往我产品里塞垃圾"的问题。Reddit 是个社区，里面有人们真实的、authentic 的观点，而且它被社区重度管理，而社区非常擅长管理它。所以对增长人员来说，最明显的策略就是："咱们造一堆自动化的垃圾、到处往 Reddit 上灌、让我的产品到处出现。"那就是增长思维，说得通，就是那种 hustle 思维。所以人们在看什么？他们在看创建几百个假的 Reddit 账号、假装成不是你自己的人。我一个人，我要造 100 个 Reddit 账号。我要自动发评论、然后给自己评论点赞。然后攒一个信任分，然后到处喊"我的产品是最好的产品"。幸好，那不太管用，但那就是最明显的策略。所以我们看到人们在试那个，然后我们也看到那些账号被封、那些评论被删。所以我们看到人们在试着灌垃圾、而且不成功，所以那是一种策略。另一种策略是：Reddit 的整个目的，就是发出来自真实用户、有用、高质量、authentic 的评论。所以在 Webflow，我们有几个 Webflow 的人去评论区说："这是我的名字，这是我工作的地方，这是一条有用的信息。"所以策略是：找到一个你想要出现的、属于某个引用来源的帖子。说你是谁、说你在哪工作，然后给一条有用的信息，那效果非常好。而如果你不是那种"我得把这规模搞到几百条评论"的增长思维，这听起来很简单。但你其实不需要 1 万条评论，哪怕 5 条都可能很好，而且它扩得非常好。所以 Reddit 策略就是那个最明显的策略：做一个 Reddit 的真正用户。开个账号、说你是谁、说你在哪工作，给一个有用的回答。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We had the early-growth leader from Deel, D-E-E-L, on the podcast a while ago. And this is how they grew initially, before AI even came around, just going big on Reddit and answering people's questions. (00:19:07): And like, "Hey, happens to be Deel. Can I help you with this problem?" So that's interesting. It's so interesting that Reddit is what is keeping ChatGPT from being spammed with stuff. It's not that ChatGPT is stopping the spam, its Reddit is just really good at that.
turns.zh: 我们之前请过 Deel（D-E-E-L）的早期增长负责人上播客。他们最初就是这么增长的——在 AI 出现之前，就是在 Reddit 上大力投入、回答人们的问题。就像"嘿，碰巧我是 Deel 的。这个问题我能帮你吗？"所以那很有意思。特别有意思的是，是 Reddit 在阻止 ChatGPT 被垃圾灌满。不是 ChatGPT 在阻止垃圾，而是 Reddit 自己就特别擅长这个。

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: I think that in a sense, ChatGPT is policing because ChatGPT is running a search, it's finding citations. There's a search algorithm that's trying to select which citations are useful. There are people at ChatGPT who are tuning their search algorithm to select which sources they trust. (00:19:40): I'm sure that there's a search evaluation team saying, "Do I like these citations, yes, no? Is Reddit showing up? I want it to show up." So I think that there are actual people at ChatGPT who are intentionally configuring their algorithm to use Reddit because it's trusted. And if it wasn't trusted, they wouldn't use it. (00:19:57): Same with Google. Google has specifically configured their search algorithm to rank Reddit and Twitter and Quora, because they want user-generated content. And if it wasn't good content, then they would change the algorithm and they wouldn't rank it. So I think that they are policing it in a sense.
turns.zh: 我觉得在某种意义上，ChatGPT 是在做审核（policing），因为 ChatGPT 在跑一个搜索、在找引用来源。有个搜索算法在试图挑出哪些引用是有用的。ChatGPT 里有人在做搜索算法的调优，来挑选他们信任哪些来源。我敢肯定有个搜索评估团队在说："我喜欢这些引用吗，喜欢还是不喜欢？Reddit 出现了吗？我想让它出现。"所以我觉得 ChatGPT 里真有那样的人，是故意把他们的算法配置成用 Reddit 的，因为它被信任。如果它不被信任，他们就不会用它。Google 也一样。Google 专门配置了他们的搜索算法，让 Reddit、Twitter、Quora 排得好，因为他们想要用户生成内容。如果那不是好内容，他们就会改算法、就不会让它排得好。所以我觉得他们在某种意义上是在做审核。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Got it. And all of this is post-training, search-oriented features of these models. It's not data they are trained on, is that right?
turns.zh: 明白了。而所有这些，都是这些模型在训练之后、面向搜索的功能。不是它们训练时所用的数据，对吧？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: I would assume that so there's the core model and then there's RAG. So the core model is I'm looking at common crawl on billions of web pages, and then I'm retraining the model. And if you ask something like, "What's the capital of California?" It predicts the next word, which is Sacramento. And that's based on the core algorithm, which is next-word prediction. (00:20:44): Then there's RAG and RAG basically means search, retrieval-augmented generation. So I'm going to do a search and then I'm going to summarize the search. There are these two different things. And so most of what I'm describing is about the RAG piece, not the core model piece. To influence the core model is probably extremely hard and maybe you'll see the impact a year later. (00:21:03): And it's probably something, some sort of obscure thing that nobody would want to do, like make a million pages that say, "Best product for X is brand." Which I don't think most people want to spend their time on. So I'm mostly focused on the RAG side, because that's the main thing that's controllable. (00:21:18): And I think also the LLM is probably not going to say your product if it didn't show up anywhere on the RAG. So I think that's where most of the interesting stuff is from an optimization perspective.

turns.zh: 首先，我会搞清楚我想为哪些问题排上名。我怎么搞清楚我想为哪些问题排上名呢？我会拿我的搜索数据。我也许会拿我的付费搜索数据，比如"我的赚钱词（money terms）是什么？我竞品的赚钱词是什么？"所以如果我是 Rippling，Deel.com 在他们的付费搜索上都竞了哪些词？然后我会把它们变成问题。其实你可以直接把这些关键词丢给 ChatGPT，说"把这些变成问题"，它做得相当好。所以拿你竞品的付费搜索数据、或者我的、或者你自己的，丢进 ChatGPT，拿到问题。这是第一步。第二步是追踪它们，所以把它们放进一个 AEO 追踪器、一个答案追踪器。第三件事是：现在谁作为引用来源出现？然后对每个不同的引用来源组有对应的策略。然后做你自己的落地页。那么现在出现的都是些什么样的落地页？是清单体（listicle）？是分类页？是文章、工具页？搞清楚哪种页面类型出现得最多，然后你为那个做一个自己的页面。你怎么让你的页面排上名？回答所有后续问题。那么人们可能会问的所有后续问题是什么？你可以回到你的搜索数据，找你 SEO 主题里那些关键词的组和主题。AEO 主题也一样。然后在站外，对每个组有不同的策略。我想说，视公司而定，雇一个 affiliate 来提你，如果你有钱的话那相当容易。所以如果你要当最好的信用卡，你付钱给 Forbes，然后你就是最好的信用卡。所以那是策略一，贵、容易、可控。YouTube、Vimeo 策略其实也相当容易，因为没有什么社区会说"我不喜欢你的 YouTube 视频"。你做一个 YouTube 视频，你爱怎么弄怎么弄。也许有人看、也许没人看，但你可以做一个 YouTube 视频或者 Vimeo 视频。而这有意思的地方在于，尤其对 B2B 来说，YouTube、Vimeo、其他视频网站，人们做视频的内容都是食物、旅行、好玩、美妆。关于"AI 驱动的支付处理 API"的视频没那么多——虽然那很有意思，但那是个很棒的赚钱机会。所以如果你为这些真的非常具体、高 LTV、可能不那么光鲜的关键词、问题、主题做个视频，那其实是个大机会。然后是 Reddit，我刚提了我们在 Webflow 做的，就是开个 Reddit 账号、说你是谁、说你在哪工作、给一个有用的回答。那个稍微棘手一点，因为社区可能会说"我不喜欢你的回答"。所以你没法保证你的评论在那儿，但它容易，所以我会做那一组。哦，还有实验设计，看什么管用。SEO 和 AEO 都有个有意思的地方：大多数信息和最佳实践其实是不正确的。原因就是人们不做分析。有人说了句什么，然后就被重复，然后它变成了最佳实践，而从来没人做过分析。所以你做了我刚说的所有事。做个实验，看它管不管用。也许我说的话一半管用、一半不管用。做你自己的实验。大多数最佳实践、大多数博客文章都是不对的。所以你怎么搭一个实验？你拿到你的问题，打开追踪，给几周时间。做你的改动，弄一个测试组、一个对照组。对测试组做干预、做你的改动，看图表有没有上去，看对照组有没有上去，现在你就知道你那个特定策略管用了。所以我绝对会做实验，而且我不会假设网上读到的东西是对的。然后你需要一个团队，那你的团队是谁？大概就是你的 SEO 团队、或者你的 SEO 代理、或者你的 SEO 顾问。大概、希望他们能做这些事，但我觉得难招的是站外那块。大多数 SEO 的人不擅长做 YouTube 视频和 Reddit 策略，所以那你可能得找另一个人。那可能是一个社区通才型的市场人员。所以基本上就是你的 SEO 团队，"现在请做答案引擎优化"。然后营销社区团队，"请帮我在更多引用来源里出现"。

turns.en: Yeah, so there's answer tracking, which is like keyword tracking. So keyword tracking would be best growth podcast, and you put that in a keyword tracking tool. (00:34:25): So if you ask the same question, you will have different answers each time. If you ask a question, there's different answers per run. And so ChatGPT is basically calculating a distribution of all the potential answers it would give. (00:34:46): You also have question variants, so you can ask different versions of the same question, and you might show up in one and you might not show up in another. And that's answer tracking. So then where do you get answer tracking? And answer tracking is essentially an evolution of keyword tracking. So we have a page with 60 different answer tracking tools. (00:35:22): But it's ultimately just like keyword tracking, it's all the same thing roughly. And so pick one of the 60, we have answer tracking, we're building answer tracking. There's 59 other options, probably all pretty good, probably all pretty similar, but pick one. My general suggestion is pick the cheapest one that does what you need. (00:35:41): Just like keyword tracking, you can only, there's not a premium version of keyword tracking. You rank number three or you don't. So pick the keyword tracker that is the cheapest that does what you want. Same with the answer tracking. And so then when I'm doing the experiment, put your answers in, track them, see a chart over time, see your average rank. (00:35:58): How often are you showing up and what's your average rank? And then you make a change, and then hopefully you go up.
turns.zh: 对，所以有"答案追踪"，就像关键词追踪。关键词追踪就是"最好的增长播客"，你把它放进一个关键词追踪工具。这种工具有 100 个，都一个样，你看你排没排上名。也许你排上了，希望你排第一。在答案里就很不一样，但它是相关的。如果你问同一个问题，每次都会有不同的答案。如果你问一个问题，每次运行都有不同的答案。所以 ChatGPT 基本上是在计算它会给出的所有潜在答案的一个分布。而取决于你什么时候问它，它基本就像一个加权的随机样本，所以你会得到不同的答案。你还有问题变体，所以你可以问同一个问题的不同版本，而你可能会在一个版本里出现、在另一个里不出现。然后有不同的"界面"（surface），有 Perplexity、有 Gemini、有 ChatGPT、有 Meta AI，所以这些界面有不同的答案。所以你本质上需要在所有这些不同的东西上建立一个"声量份额"（share of voice），就像一个分布。我出现的频率多高？我的平均排名是多少？那就是答案追踪。那你去哪找答案追踪？答案追踪本质上是关键词追踪的进化。所以我们有个页面列了 60 个不同的答案追踪工具。但它归根结底就跟关键词追踪一样，大致都是同一回事。所以从那 60 个里挑一个，我们有答案追踪、我们在建答案追踪。还有 59 个其他选项，大概都挺好、大概都挺像，但挑一个。我的一般建议是挑那个最便宜、又能做你需要的事的。就像关键词追踪，你没法——关键词追踪没有高级版。你排第三或者没排上，就那样。所以挑那个最便宜、又能做你想要的事的关键词追踪器。答案追踪也一样。所以当我做实验时，把你的答案放进去、追踪它们、看一张随时间变化的图、看你的平均排名。你出现的频率多高、你的平均排名是多少？然后你做一个改动，然后希望你上去了。

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: So interestingly, there are similar, foundational algorithms across all of these. They're all using search, they're all using search, and they're all using LLMs, which foundational algorithms are all the same. The results are actually pretty different. So we're doing a study, we're seeing that Google and Bing are not that similar search engines. (00:36:41): We're seeing that ChatGPT citations and Google Search results are actually not that similar. Perplexity is interestingly more similar to Google than ChatGPT. We did a study looking at thousands of questions and saw the citation overlap with Google Search results was around 35% for ChatGPT and Google, so not that much. (00:37:02): Perplexity was around 70%, but essentially they're all similar algorithms, but with very different citations and results. So then look at which surfaces have the most traffic and then track those. You probably don't need to track all of them, but look across all those. (00:37:17): But you do need to look at your share of voice or the percent of time you show up across all these surfaces. You need to ask the question multiple times, and you need to ask the variance of the question to truly know how frequently you're showing up.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，所有这些背后有相似的基础算法。它们都在用搜索、也都在用 LLM，所以它们的基础算法都一样。但结果其实挺不一样的。我们在做一个研究，发现 Google 和 Bing 并不是那么像的搜索引擎。我们发现 ChatGPT 的引用来源和 Google 搜索结果其实没那么像。Perplexity 有意思的是，它比 ChatGPT 更像 Google。我们分析了几千个问题，发现 ChatGPT 和 Google 的引用重叠大约是 35%，所以没那么多。Perplexity 大约是 70%，但本质上它们都是相似的算法，只是引用和结果非常不同。所以然后看哪些界面流量最大、然后追踪那些。你可能不需要追踪所有，但要横扫所有这些看一眼。但你确实需要看你的声量份额、或者你在这些界面里出现的时长百分比。你需要把问题问很多次，而且你需要问这个问题的不同变体，才能真正知道你出现的频率。

turns.zh: 意思是，B2B 出现的引用来源和市集（marketplaces）出现的，是不同种类的引用来源。对 B2B，可能就像我问问题时 TechRadar 出现得特别多。我从没读过 TechRadar，但不知为何它总出现。我肯定它很好。但 TechRadar 因为某种原因在 B2B 里出现得特别多。在电商里不会是那个，会是 Glamour 和 Cosmopolitan。对市集，会是 Eater、Yelp、TripAdvisor 那种地方，所以出现的引用来源种类是不同的。我聊的大部分东西是特指 B2B 的，跟电商不一样。对大多数 B2B 问题，答案是不可点击的。没什么可点的。所以如果你真想衡量影响，你不能只看最后触点的引荐流量。你得用追踪看自己是不是在答案里出现了。然后你还得问用户"转化之后你是怎么听说我们的"，才能真正知道影响。所以对 B2B 来说更难追踪。还有对 B2B，你可能是在 50 个触点之后才决定用哪个工资管理软件。对品牌来说，不会是你刚搜个什么、就突然在工资管理软件上花 10 万美金。所以那是 B2B。电商不同，电商现在其实有更多可点击的卡片，就像你在 Google 里那样。所以如果你问"公寓用最好的电视是哪个？"会有真正的可购物卡片。那些可购物卡片展示多个卖家。那些卖家有富媒体摘要（rich snippets）。Schema 重要，评论数重要，所以其实相当不同。你可以看最后触点的引荐流量，来很好地感知你拿到的转化数。对电商，餐厅、酒店、本地市集也类似，那块类似。然后我想说早期公司也不同。所以我之前提过，早期我的建议是根本不要做 SEO。对答案引擎优化，绝对要做 AEO，而且只做引用优化和长尾。不要做任何中间那段 SEO 的东西，只要被引用、回答那些真的非常具体的问题。

turns.en: Yes. And I would give the same answer that Brian Balfour gave on your previous episode on this, which is that it's not your choice whether to play the game. You are playing the game whether you want to or not, so you might as well try to show up. If you just say, "Don't look at any of my data," then you cannot show up and your competitors will. (00:42:27): Now, what you can do is you can say, "I don't want you to train on my data, so you can index my site, but please don't train on my data." And they have different user agents for that and different bots, so you can just say, "And we're building a Webflow app to block training but not indexation." (00:50:01): So the slope of the curve is unusually steep, and the shape of the curve is also very unusual. turns.zh: Ethan，我就说，我从这期对话里学到太多了，真有意思。我看得出，你多爱这事儿一目了然，而且你钻得又深又 nerdy。跟一个对这些东西钻得这么深、懂得这么多的人聊，就是好玩，所以谢谢你跟我们分享所有这些。我要换个稍微不同的方向了。有个整块的世界是 AI 内容——人们用 AI 生成内容、生成落地页。就像"天哪，SEO 再也不用自己生成所有这些东西了。AI 会让所有这些东西更容易。"你们做了一个很大的研究，关于那怎么运作、用 AI 生成内容是不是个好主意。你能聊聊你从那学到的，以及人们应该怎么看待 AI 在生成内容这件事上？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: Yes. So I remember when ChatGPT launched and Brian Balfour posted on LinkedIn, "What do you people think that is going to happen from ChatGPT and AI?" And my immediate response is spam, so just lots and lots of spam, especially SEO spam. And then there was a whole industry around AI-generated content, and I knew immediately that it wouldn't work. (00:52:20): And the reason why I knew it wouldn't work, and when I say AI-generated content, I mean automated content with no human-in-the-loop. So I think that the future of content is clearly AI-assisted. Clearly, you and I will be using AI to help us write, so it's not no AI at all, but it's not 100% generated with AI. I immediately knew that it wouldn't work. (00:52:38): Why did I know that? I knew that because I created spam in 2007, and I knew what Google did about it and how, and I knew the exact same thing was going to happen. So what I did in 2007 is I and all the other shopping comparison people scraped all each other's content, reviews, chopped it up, scraped content, 100 million search pages, snippets, and it worked really well. (00:53:02): And then it stopped working, and then all those companies disappeared. I knew that was exactly what's going to happen with AI-generated content. And so from the beginning, I've not focused on AI-generated content. Many people have, but I don't know, so maybe it does work. There's lots of case studies about it working. (00:53:20): So let's do the study, let's do an analysis. So we took, we looked at both Google and at ChatGPT where we took thousands of searches and thousands of questions, and we put those searches into Google Search. We put those questions into chat and the ChatGPT, and then we looked at the citations or the Google Search results. Then we looked at an AI detector. (00:53:43): So we used Surfer SEO's AI detector. Now, when I tell people this, they say, "Well, you can't detect AI." So then we evaluated the efficacy and the accuracy of the AI detector. So we did that by generating thousands of AI-generated articles and it was very predictive. And then we looked at real articles, we did that two different ways. (00:54:05): One way is we write real articles, and the other is we took a random sample of 100,000 URLs from Common Crawl over the last five years. And then we looked at the AI detector before ChatGPT was launched, so it necessarily was content not created by a human. And then the false positive rate was around 8%, so basically the AI detector is very accurate. (00:54:29): So we took that, then we ran it on the content. So then what we saw was around 10% to 12% of content in Google Search, and then ChatGPT or AI-generated, 90% are not. And we ran a correlation analysis showing the exact same thing. So we essentially did a very rigorous study showing that AI content does not work. AI-assisted content edited is great. (00:54:52): We do that sometimes, other people do that, that is clearly the future of content. So that does work and should work and that's good, but purely 100% AI-generated does not work. So then the second thing that we did was we found that, this was unexpected, but we found that there's more AI-generated content on the internet than human-generated content. (00:55:13): So back to the Common Crawl study, we looked at 100,000 different URLs over the past five years. And then you can see this curve where AI-generated is now higher than human-created. So there's more AI-generated content on the internet than human-generated content, which is disturbing. So then let's say that AI-generated content did work. (00:55:32): If AI-generated content worked, then everyone would do it. Just like in 2007, shopping comparison sites, if I can scrape my content, why would I pay anyone to write it? I'll just scrape it from you and I'll chop it up. So then everyone will do that, and then it will go from most content is AI-generated to almost all of the content is AI-generated. (00:55:51): Then what will happen if that works, is that Google now becomes a search engine for ChatGPT responses. So if Google's a search engine for ChatGPT responses, there's no reason for Google to exist. Just go to ChatGPT, which is the exact same thing that happened in 2007. (00:56:04): Google said, "I see all these shopping comparison search engines showing up in my search results. So I'm essentially a search engine for search engines." I should be showing the TV in my results. I shouldn't be showing other vertical search engines, so I'm going to get rid of them and I'm just going to go straight to the product. (00:56:23): The same thing will be true for ChatGPT. Now for ChatGPT, let's say that ChatGPT ranks its own derivatives in its citations, so then you have this infinite loop of derivatives. So I go to ChatGPT, I say, "Generate 10 articles." I put those articles into the citations and then I say, "Summarize these citations that were derivative." (00:56:41): And then I keep on doing derivatives of derivatives, and then you have an infinite loop of derivatives, and now AI is summarizing itself. There's a paper about this called Model Collapse. So again, there's the core algorithm and then there's the RAG piece. So the core algorithm, a group did a study showing model collapse, which was what if you feed in AI derivatives into the model and train the core model on the derivatives? (00:57:06): And then what happened was you had all these problems, hallucinations, things break very quickly. Okay. So then we did a study on what if you feed derivatives into the RAG piece? So generate 10 derivatives, put that into RAG, summarize that. And then generate 10 more, and then summarize my summarizations, infinite loop of derivatives. What happens? (00:57:25): And so what happens is there's a wisdom of the crowd. The LLM is summarizing the opinion of many people. So if you ask a question like, "What's the best flavor of ice cream?" There's not one answer, there's thousands of opinions. So the LLM is summarizing these many, many opinions in this wisdom of the crowd. (00:57:40): And the wisdom of the crowd basically says that, "If you take the average of a large group of people, their average response will be better than the best single individual in the group." And so it's better to have more diversity of opinions, wisdom of the crowd. So what happens to the infinite loop of derivatives? You essentially converge on one opinion. (00:58:00): So if you ask, "What's the best flavor of ice cream?" It will eventually say, "It's vanilla and it's only vanilla, and there's no other flavor of ice cream." And so that's a simple example, but if you feed in derivatives of derivatives into the model, you'll basically take the wisdom of the crowd. (00:58:15): And that will shrink and you'll have a single opinion on everything, which is really bad. So that's what happens if AI content, 100% unassisted AI content works.

生成的文章，而且它预测得很准。然后我们看真实文章，我们用两种不同方式做。一种是我们写真实文章，另一种是我们从 Common Crawl 里取了过去五年 10 万个 URL 的随机样本。然后我们看 ChatGPT 发布之前的 AI 检测器——那必然是真人写的内容。然后误报率大约是 8%，所以基本上这个 AI 检测器非常准。所以我们拿了那个，然后把它跑在内容上。然后我们看到的是：Google 生成内容管用，那人人都会去做。就像 2007 年，购物比价网站，如果我能爬你的内容，我为什么还要付钱让人写？我直接从你那爬、切碎就完了。所以然后人人都会那么做，然后内容就会从"大多是 AI 生成"变成"几乎全是 AI 生成"。然后如果那管用，会发生什么？Google 就会变成一个给 ChatGPT 回复用的搜索引擎。所以如果 Google 是给 ChatGPT 回复用的搜索引擎，那 Google 就没理由存在了。直接去 ChatGPT 就好了——这正是 2007 年发生的完全一样的事。Google 说"我看到所有这些购物比价搜索引擎出现在我的搜索结果里。所以我本质上是个给搜索引擎用的搜索引擎。我的结果里应该直接展示电视，我不该展示其他垂直搜索引擎，所以我要把它们干掉、直接去产品。"对 ChatGPT 也一样。假设 ChatGPT turns.en: Number one is Emotional Intelligence, and people talk about the concept of emotional intelligence, but there's actual research and psychology around that. turns.zh: 第一本是《情商》（Emotional Intelligence），人们聊情商这个概念，但那背后其实有真正的研究和心理学。我相信它是 80 年代出版的，但有本很好的书总结了关于情商的奠基性研究。而在建立关系、跟人沟通时理解他们的情绪，它非常有用。所以那是第一本。还有做增长，因为增长就是让人们用你的东西。所以如果你有框架来推断人们会怎么用你的东西，那你就能成为更有效的增长人员。这就引出我的第二本书，Cialdini 的说服（Persuasion）那本。Robert Cialdini 写了一系列关于说服的书，但同样，他有关于怎么说服人注册、购买的框架。他把他的框架拆开讲，而且同样，它基于心理学。我觉得尤其在增长里，有各种各样的心理学研究和行为经济学研究可以指导测试。如果你只读《思考，快与慢》《说服力》《情商》，你基本就能拿那些框架、用各种方式应用到增长上。然后最后一本是《如何度量任何事》（How to Measure Anything）。《如何度量任何事》是关于度量那些不是一眼就能度量的事。他们给的例子是，他们想度量一个管弦乐队指挥有多好，而他们可以发问卷、或者看每个指挥得到的起立鼓掌次数。起立鼓掌越多大概意味着这个更好，而你不需要去问卷任何人。但增长的很多事、商业的很多事，都不是一眼就知道怎么度量的，但任何事都能被度量，所以那是我第三本。

turns.zh: 心流，真是个有趣的小缩影，说明你为什么这么擅长这个。

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith

turns.zh: 这个相机和这个麦克风。我买了个 Sony 无反单反（mirrorless SLR），我忘了具体型号。但，抱歉，弄一个带广角镜头的无反单反，真的能彻底改变你的视频通话。然后我有这个 Shure 麦克风，我觉得大概 180 美金。这极大提升了我视频通话的质量。而且我喜欢设计东西，你可以设计你的视频通话、让它们特别棒。你可以在背景放花，这儿来点，一些向日葵。

turns.en: Your background is quite exquisite and I didn't mention that, but it looks beautiful. Okay, two more questions. (01:07:13): Do you have a life motto that you find really useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 你的背景相当精致，我没提那个，但看起来很美。好，还有两个问题。你有没有一个人生格言，觉得在工作或生活里真的有用？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: There's the Outliers book about 10,000 hours. And the themes there are you don't have to be the smartest, you have to be sufficiently smart, number one. Number two is focused practice, so it's not just trying hard, it's doing it in an intentional, focused way. And the third thing is lots of practice, so no one can master anything because they're a genius. (01:07:44): They master it because they spent a significant amount of time practicing and they practice in an intentional way. And so my motto is essentially a combination of those things, which is that I'm not going to necessarily win because my brain is the largest brain or that I tried the hardest. (01:08:00): It's because I'm going to be the most intentional about my practice, and I'm going to be as intense as I possibly can be about that practice.
turns.zh: 有《异类》（Outliers）那本关于一万小时的书。那里的主题是：你不必是最聪明的，你只要足够聪明，第一。第二是有聚焦的练习，所以不只是努力试，而是以一种有意图、聚焦的方式去做。第三是大量的练习，所以没人能因为自己是天才就精通任何事。他们精通，是因为他们花了大量时间练习、而且是以有意图的方式练习。所以我的格言本质上是这些东西的组合，也就是：我不见得会赢，因为我的脑子最大、或者我努力得最狠。而是因为我对我的练习会最有意图，而且我会对那个练习尽可能 intense。

turns.en: That's amazing. I don't know if butter lettuce has been mentioned on this podcast before. Ethan, this was incredible. This was everything I was hoping it'd be. (01:09:09): Two final questions, where can folks find you if they want to potentially work with you guys? And how can listeners be useful to you?
turns.zh: 那太神了。我知道我不知道黄油生菜以前在这档播客里有没有被提到过。Ethan，这期太了不起了。这就是我希望它成为的样子。我觉得我们刚把大家对 SEO 和 AEO 到底在发生什么的认知拉高了一个层级？忘了 GEO 吧。最后两个问题，如果人们想可能跟你们合作，能在哪找到你？以及听众怎么帮到你？

turns.speaker: Ethan Smith
turns.en: So where you can find me, number one, is on LinkedIn. I spend lots of time on LinkedIn and I publish original, so we do original research. We have a whole research team hypothesizing and evaluating those hypotheses. So we publish, all the studies that I mentioned, we publish on our site and I publish them on LinkedIn. (01:09:33): So follow me on LinkedIn, add me on LinkedIn, send me a message. LinkedIn, number one, and then number two is we have a blog which we call The 5%. So /5%, which stands for 5% of work, 5% of landing pages drive almost all the impact, so that's the theme. This is only useful stuff. So our blog at 5%, you could subscribe to our email and to our studies. And then how can people be useful to me? (01:09:58): So I spent time thinking about this and there's two ways people can help me. The first way is that there's not that much research around what works in AEO, and I would love to know what people are testing and what the results are and what works. So people doing studies and publishing that are sending it to me, I would love as much analysis and research as possible, number one. (01:10:20): Then the second one is to help me on LinkedIn by commenting on my posts and on my comments. So you posted most recently the Brian Balfour episode, for which I wrote a long, thoughtful comment, and then I got about 25 likes and then I got responses to that. And so I've been commenting on other people's LinkedIn posts and I've been writing these long LinkedIn posts. (01:10:43): And when people comment, it boosts the engagement within LinkedIn and then I get mass distribution. So the more people and thoughtful comments, so not this is great, but a long, thoughtful comment that stimulates conversation. So if people comment on my posts, then I'm just going to blow up on LinkedIn and I might be as big as you someday.
turns.zh: 所以你能找到我的地方，第一，是 LinkedIn。我花大量时间在 LinkedIn 上，而且我发原创内容，我们做原创研究。我们有整个研究团队在做假设、然后评估那些假设。所以我们发布——我提到的所有研究，我们发在我们网站上，我也发在 LinkedIn 上。所以在 LinkedIn 上关注我、加我、给我发消息。LinkedIn，第一，然后第二是我们有个博客，我们叫它 The 5%。就是 /5%，代表 5% 的工作、5% 的落地页驱动了几乎全部的影响，所以那是主题。这里只有有用的东西。所以我们的 5% 博客，你可以订阅我们的邮件和我们的研究。然后人们怎么帮到我？我花时间想过这个，人们能用两种方式帮我。第一种是，关于 AEO 里什么管用的研究还不多，而我很想知道人们在测什么、结果是什么、什么管用。所以人们做研究、发布出来、发给我，我想要尽可能多的分析和研究，第一。第二种是在 LinkedIn 上帮我——在我的帖子下评论、在我评论下评论。你最近发了 Brian Balfour 那期，我就写了条长而走心的评论，然后我大概得了 25 个赞、然后收到了对它的回复。所以我一直在别人 LinkedIn 帖子下评论、也一直在写那些长的 LinkedIn 帖子。而当人们评论，它会在 LinkedIn 内推高互动，然后我就得到海量分发。所以越多人、越多走心的评论——不是"这真棒"那种，而是能激发对话的长而走心的评论。所以如果人们在我的帖子下评论，那我就要在 LinkedIn 上爆了，说不定哪天跟你一样大。
